cues.text: Good afternoon, Dave, come on in and take a seat.
cues.speaker: Dr Green

cues.text: Hi, Dr Green thanks
cues.speaker: Dave

cues.text: Hang on a minute, I'll just find the first draft ot your project paper and we can have a look at it together. Now yours is the one on Work Placement, isn't it?
cues.speaker: Dr Green

cues.text: Yeah, that's right.
cues.speaker: Dave

cues.text: So what made you choose that for your project?
cues.speaker: Dr Green

cues.text: Well, l suppose it was because sending students off to various companies for work experience seems to be such a typical part of educational courses these days - I mean, even school kids get to do it.
cues.speaker: Dave

cues.text: But I felt everyone just kind of assumes it's a good thing and l guess I wanted to find out if that's the case.
cues.speaker: Dave

cues.text: But you don't look at schools or colleges, right? You've stuck to university placement schemes.
cues.speaker: Dr Green

cues.text: Yeah, well, I quickly found that I had to limit my research, otherwise the area was just too big. Do you think that was OK?
cues.speaker: Dave

cues.text: I think it's very sensible, especially as the objectives might be very different. So how many schemes did you look at?
cues.speaker: Dr Green

cues.text: Well, I sent out about 150 questionnaires altogether - you know. 50 of each to university authorities, students and companies, and I got responses from 15 educational institutions, and. er, 30 students in 11 individual companies.
cues.speaker: Dave

cues.text: Great, that sounds like a good sample. And who did you send your company questionnaires to?
cues.speaker: Dr Green

cues.text: Well, the idea was to have them done by the students’ Line Managers, but sometimes they were filled in by the Human Resources manager or even the owner of the company.
cues.speaker: Dave

cues.text: Right. I didn’t find a full list anywhere, so I think it's very important to provide that, really. You can put it as an appendix at the back.
cues.speaker: Dr Green

cues.text: Right. I've got a record of all the respondents so that'll be easy. I hope other things were OK. I mean I’ve already put such a lot of work into this project, identifying the companies and so on.
cues.speaker: Dave

cues.text: Oh, I can tell I think you've done a good job overall.
cues.speaker: Dr Green

cues.text: I thought your questionnaires were excellent, and you'd obviously done lots of background reading, but there were a few problems with the introduction. First of all, I think you need to make some slight changes to the organisation of your information there, at present it's a bit confused.
cues.speaker: Dr Green

cues.text: OK. What did you have in mind?
cues.speaker: Dave

cues.text: Well, you write quite a bit about Work Placement in general, but you never explain what you mean by the term.
cues.speaker: Dr Green

cues.text: So you think I should give a definition?
cues.speaker: Dave

cues.text: Exactly. And the introduction is the place to do it. And then look, you start talking about what's been written on the topic - but it's all a bit mixed up with your own project.
cues.speaker: Dr Green

cues.text: So do you think it would be better to have two sections there like, a survey of the literature as the introduction and then a separate section on the aims of my research?
cues.speaker: Dave

cues.text: I do. You can include your methods for collecting data in the second section too. It would be much dearer for your reader .. you know, establish the background first, then how your work relates to it, it would flow quite nicely then.
cues.speaker: Dr Green

cues.text: Yes, I see what you mean
cues.speaker: Dave

cues.text: Anyway, moving on I like the way you've grouped your findings into three main topic areas.
cues.speaker: Dr Green

cues.text: Well, it became very obvious from the questionnaires that the preparation stage was really important for the whole scheme to work. So had to look at that first. And I found a huge variation between the different institutions, as you saw.
cues.speaker: Dave

cues.text: I was wondering if you could give a summary at the end of this stage of what you consider to be the best practice you found, I think that would be very helpful.
cues.speaker: Dr Green

cues.text: Right, I'll just make a note of that What did you think of my second set of findings - on Key Skills development? For me, this is the core of my whole project really ...
cues.speaker: Dave

cues.text: And you've handled it very well. I wouldn't want you to make any changes you've already got a nice final focus on good practice there.
cues.speaker: Dr Green

cues.text: Thanks.
cues.speaker: Dave

cues.text: Right, now I think the last part, which deals with the reasons why students don't learn ...
cues.speaker: Dr Green

cues.text: What? The constraints on learning chapter?
cues.speaker: Dave

cues.text: Yes. that's the one I think you need to refer to the evidence from your research a bit more closely here.
cues.speaker: Dr Green

cues.text: Yon know, maybe you could illustrate it with quotations from the questionnaires, or even use any extracts from a student 'diary' if you can. And refer back to what you've written about good practice ...
cues.speaker: Dr Green
